chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a mukātab who pays half of his mukātabah contract, and the other half remains due from him, then he calls his masters to the rest of his contract and says to them: Take what remains in a single payment. He said: They take what remains, then he is emancipated.

And he said regarding a mukātab who pays part of his mukātabah contract, then dies, leaving a son and leaving wealth greater than what he still owes from his mukātabah contract: His masters are to be paid what remains of his mukātabah contract, and whatever remains belongs to his child.

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: a slave under a contractual agreement to purchase his freedom
key_terms.لِوَلَدِهِ: belonging to his child as inheritance
key_terms.مَوَالِيَهُ: his masters who hold the contract over him
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: his manumission contract and its financial obligation
key_terms.يَمُوتُ: he dies before completing the contract

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mukātab pays part of his contract and then offers the rest at once or dies before completing payment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the mukātab, a slave under a contract of emancipation. It establishes that the remaining contract amount may be accepted in a single payment for manumission, and that if the mukātab dies leaving sufficient wealth, the balance is paid to the masters and the remainder passes to his son.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3485 - Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Abu al-Sabbah, from Abu Abdullah (as),

regarding a mukatab (a slave under a contract of emancipation) who pays half of his contract and still owes the remaining half. Then he offers his masters the remaining amount as a lump sum payment.
Imam (as) said: "They may take the remaining amount, and he becomes free."

And regarding a mukatab who pays part of his contract, then dies, leaving behind a son and wealth greater than the amount owed for his contract:
Imam (as) said: "The masters are paid the remaining balance of the contract, and whatever remains belongs to his son."
